findings.detail: The saved audit is a dated 40-service snapshot. Its README explains that coupang-retail/catalog.search was registered later, bringing HEAD to 41. This is a documented scope change, not a defect; all 14 assigned services and their capability counts were included.

The old 403 receipt is service oliveyoung/catalog.product_detail and tests only the mobile document HTML path; it has no cookie or authorization and is tagged document_html_attempt_only. The oliveyoung-public manifest separately says its /goods/api/v1/detail contract is uncaptured and warns that 403 does not prove a customer-login requirement. Keep this as an HTML-path diagnostic, not proof that the public API or entire Oliveyoung service is down.

Partner API blocked states are tied to missing credential/entitlement prerequisites; this audit made no request for those endpoints, so they are not measured server 403/5xx failures. Public Printful feed and public consumer readers are separated from credentialed APIs.

Old public receipts are explicitly historical and tied to source hashes. Sample notes scope results to one query/product/category or bounded pages; Oliveyoung KR and aggregate commerce/Ulta common-collector receipts with changed hashes are needs_reverification rather than fresh PASS.

findings.detail: Initial request was HTTP 200 application/json with query serum and page-size hint 10, but the maintained client returned SEPHORA_SEARCH_SCHEMA_INVALID. In-memory diagnosis showed a matching keyword, valid normalized product rows, 60 products, and totalProducts=745. Root cause was a fixed 60-row source page despite the smaller hint, not a 403 or outage. The later maintained CLI replay succeeded for one page (60/745, maxPages=1, incomplete); continuation-size and independent-query reuse behavior are covered by 22 local tests only.

currentPublicChecks.interpretation: Field shape, query echo, and normalized product-row contract were valid; the client rejected only because this endpoint returned 60 products despite the requested size hint 10. One diagnostic call had a local summary/capture error after the response; no raw response body was retained. This is schema/page-width drift, not HTTP 403.

The maintained CLI replay verified one page of 60 normalized results against a reported 745 results. maxPages=1 made the run intentionally incomplete; this is not live evidence of complete pagination. This replay preceded the later continuation-only request-width refinements, which were validated locally without another remote request.

implementationChanges.rootCause: The anonymous search endpoint returned 60 products for a page-size hint of 10, while the client treated any row count above the hint as invalid. After accepting the observed 60-row first page, continuation also had to pass that actual width; otherwise a final short page could fail validation. A client-global remembered width was removed because it could contaminate a separate query on the same client.
implementationChanges.fix: Accept only a valid fixed 60-row response within the reported total, report both requested and actual width, use the actual width for page counts, pass the first response width into continuation requests, and keep the width scoped to each operation/query.
implementationChanges.remoteReplayBoundary: The 13:17:51Z maintained CLI live replay covered one page only and ran before pagination-only follow-up refinements. Those refinements have synthetic offline coverage; no post-refinement remote replay was made.
